p1_cyber.title: Phase 1 gate: totals + spot-check 3 entries via GitHub API

layman_note.what: Verified all 5 answer keys: 167 spots, 70 CVEs, 34 CWE types. Spot-checked 3 entries (Django, curl, OpenSSL) via GitHub API — all confirmed.
layman_note.why: Phase 1 gate ensures the ground-truth data is solid before we build the scanner on top of it.
layman_note.concept: A phase gate is a quality checkpoint — you don't move forward until the data passes minimum thresholds, like checking ingredients before you start cooking.
layman_note.next: Phase 2: build a Semgrep scanner wrapper to find vulnerabilities automatically, then compare its alerts against our verified answer key.

p1_cyber.title: src/run_scanner.py Semgrep wrapper; scan vulnerable snapshot of project 1

layman_note.what: Built a Semgrep wrapper that fetches Django's pre-fix vulnerable files (via the answer key's parent commit SHAs) and scans them with a locally-pinned 10-rule ruleset. Produced 10 deterministic alerts.
layman_note.why: Phase 2 needs a real scanner's output to compare against the verified answer key later (Phase 4) -- this step gets that scanner running end to end on the first project.
layman_note.concept: The ruleset lives in the repo instead of pulling from Semgrep's online registry, so a scan today and a scan in six months on the same code give byte-identical results -- reproducibility, not just correctness.
layman_note.next: Step-008: run the same scanner on the other 4 vulnerable snapshots (curl, OpenSSL, Pillow, Node.js).
